name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets within a common framework and parameterization by converting sparse mocap markers into SMPL body model parameters with shape, pose, hand articulation, and soft-tissue dynamics. The dataset contains 42 hours of mocap data, 346 subjects, and 11,451 motions.
creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Nikolaus F. Troje; Gerard Pons-Moll; Michael J. Black
citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1, 2019.
rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by unifying 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common SMPL-based representation using MoSh++. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, several others were obtained privately, and some were recorded by the authors themselves, including Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, and SSM. The source datasets were recorded using different numbers of markers placed at different body locations, and even within a dataset the number of markers varies. For the SSM dataset used to tune and evaluate MoSh++, subjects were captured with an OptiTrack motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. The method adjusts the pose prior weight as a function of the number of missing markers in a frame.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are archival optical marker-based human motion capture datasets containing sparse marker trajectories from 15 source datasets, plus the SSM dataset containing synchronized marker-based mocap and high-resolution 4D body scans. AMASS maps these marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: When no hand markers are present on recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ maps marker-based mocap data from varying marker sets into a unified SMPL representation. Each frame includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft-tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations. The authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems caused by swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet and multiple source datasets with varying marker sets were standardized into a common format. For SSM evaluation, scan-to-model distances were computed by uniformly sampling 10,000 points from each synchronized 3D scan and measuring distance to the closest point on the reconstructed mesh. The authors also manually inspected AMASS results and corrected or held out problematic sequences with swapped or mislabeled markers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset does not describe human semantic labeling of items. Instead, MoSh++ fits a body model to sparse mocap markers in two stages to estimate latent marker locations, body shape, pose, hand pose when hand markers are present, and soft-tissue dynamics. The authors also manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Due to inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++; SMPL; SMPL-H; DMPL; MANO; Chumpy
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state that with MoSh++ it is easy to add more data, that they will continue to expand the dataset, and that they will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared. They also state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by the authors and the community.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape; hand articulation; soft-tissue motion; motion recordings; 3D body scans. The paper also states that SSM contains three subjects with varying body shapes, and two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable machine learning for applications in animation and computer vision, and to support generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The source datasets vary in marker sets and laboratory-specific procedures. The SSM dataset used for tuning and evaluation consists of only three subjects with varying body shapes, and two of the three subjects were professional models.
rai:dataLimitations: Existing mocap datasets are small and motions limited, and source datasets vary in format and kinematic structure. AMASS inherits inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, requiring manual inspection and correction or exclusion. Marker occlusion can lead to unreliable and implausible poses. The paper notes there is no ground-truth data for evaluating accuracy of hand articulation. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for machine learning applications in animation and computer vision, as well as visualization and generating training data for deep learning. It provides a unified format consisting of SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue motion. Users interested only in pose can ignore body shape and soft-tissue deformations, and users can normalize all bodies to the same shape if desired.
